Research  ·  Government AI assurance Your supplier never read the contract.

What we are watching in government and the public sector, the obligations already due or coming, and where to start.

SECTOR VIEWUPDATED 26 AUG 2026RESEARCH ONLY
What we are watching

Three questions we ask every organization in this sector.

01

Supplier obligations after onboarding

Supplier obligations are usually set when a contract is signed. We check whether they were re-scoped when the service changed, for example when a supplier added AI features or moved its hosting.

02

Residency evidenced per system

A program-wide statement that data stays in-country is easy to make. We look for evidence for each system: where it stores, processes and backs up data, and who can reach it from outside.

03

An evidence pack that predates the request

When an auditor or a ministry asks for evidence, the pack should already exist. We check whether it is kept current as systems change, so answering a request takes days instead of a project.

Obligations in force

What is already due, and what is coming.

Each obligation below is externally imposed and shown with its issuing authority and either a date or its current status. Read each one against what your organization could evidence this week, not what it plans to build.

DURING 2026UAE Cyber Security Council

Mandatory PQC migration-plan submission by government entities

An automated cryptographic inventory and a formally approved transition plan.

UAE
ROLLING OUT 2026UAE · NCAP

National Cyber Accreditation Programme restricts which providers may serve critical infrastructure

That your security and cloud suppliers hold the required accreditation.

UAE
IN FORCEDESC (Dubai)

Information Security Regulation v3: 13 security domains

Annual penetration testing, quarterly vulnerability assessment; non-compliance means removal from procurement lists.

UAE
IN FORCEUAE federal · NESA

Information Assurance Standard v2: 188 controls, 39 mandatory Priority One

Demonstrated P1 coverage across IAM, patching, data protection and incident response.

UAE
IN FORCEUAE

Secure Supply Chain Programme

Software Bill of Materials transparency for government procurement.

UAE
2024UAE · AIATC

Law No. 3 of 2024 establishing the Abu Dhabi AI and Advanced Technology Council

Program-level AI governance aligned to emirate policy.

UAE
JUN 2024UAE

Charter for the Development and Use of AI: 12 principles

Documented alignment for AI deployed in public service.

UAE
IN FORCEKSA · NCA

ECC-2:2024: 4 domains, 28 subdomains, ~110 controls

Cybersecurity roles filled by qualified Saudi nationals; data localization via NDMO.

KSA
IN FORCEQatar · NCSA

National Information Assurance policy

Information assurance controls for government agencies and critical sectors.

QATAR

In short: public bodies face post-quantum planning, supplier accreditation and AI governance obligations across the UAE, KSA and Qatar. How we work with them through accredited local partners is on the Government & public sector industry page. Last reviewed 26 Aug 2026.
